- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, true price often reverses or drops sharply; reduce forecast slope.
- After a sharp spike in model forecast, true price frequently overshoots then corrects — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer for downward correction.
- If true price deviates >5% from model in first 5–7 days, adjust forecast to mean-revert toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, if model is flat or rising slowly, true price often exhibits volatility or sudden drops — increase forecast volatility buffer.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2 spikes, model tends to overreact — apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast momentum.
